OPN-54.text:
Reads follow sharing, as simply as this:

- **RichView Cowork:** everything is private by default. The author shares a report with their organization or with anyone on the web.
- **RichView Publish (such as RichView News):** a publishing workflow that can require an editor's approval.
  - An editor's own publish lands as private; the editor makes it public before anyone sees it.
  - When an author who isn't an editor submits a report and an editor approves it, it becomes public automatically.
- **Report lists:** anyone sees only the reports shared with them, and these roles come from FEA-SF-19.

Whether a server render API exists, and how tokens work, are technical details the agents decide.
OPN-54.note: Dictated by Daniel in the review chat on 2026-10-26: "Daniel: 'if people are using our RichView CoWork… Things are private by default, and they have to share it first. They can share it with their organization, or with anyone on the web. As simple as that. If they're on RichView News, there is a publishing workflow which can require an editor to accept the publishing… it gets published as private, and you have to, as an editor, make it public before anyone sees it. And if you suggest it to editor and editor agrees to it, then it gets automatically done as public… this is the workflow' (2026-10-26, live)". Recorded by the lockdown agent at his request.

OPN-59.text:
Chosen option: Rich style files, mechanics fixed (STY-14).

Daniel's STY-14 answer: authors and agents change whatever differs between the styles, guided by safe and experimental marks; every value is validated and measured at render, so a weak result shows as a warning rather than being impossible.

OPN-62.text:
Use tabular figures wherever the font can do it. Proportional figures appear only where alignment isn't needed and the font has no tabular set.

To close that gap, RichView creates tabular-figure variants of Big Shoulders (Brutalist) and Patrick Hand (Hand-drawn), so metric values and columns in those styles also align while keeping their lettering. Both faces are under the SIL Open Font License, which allows modified versions. Any Reserved Font Name rule decides what the variants are called, and they ship under the same licence.

Proportionally, we do if not needed… the task for you is also create variation of the Big Shoulders and Patrick Hand font faces… that will have Tabular representation of values as well' (2026-10-26, live)". OPN-63.text:
Live data connectors are standard on every RichView server, Cowork and Publish, whether local or hosted. RichView builds the connector core, and PR #66's work enters it (FEA-BR-01).

- **Connectors on a server:** each server offers a set of connectors to set up. Named people manage them, and specific people are granted access to each one, under the governance roles (FEA-SF-19).
- **SQL as a data source:** a report can use SQL against a connector where today it would link to a CSV or another file.
- **Not a full CMS:** Publish's publishing setup is a light workflow (OPN-54), not a full CMS.
- **Offline HTML:** a self-contained HTML file sent around never queries live data. The one exception is a data source pointing to a URL: the file downloads the data from that address, so the data updates when what the URL points to changes. There's no warning, because the reader already trusts the sender of the HTML.
- **Credentials:** they stay in the server's configuration and never appear in `.rmd` files, report folders, rendered output, MCP arguments or agent context (ARC-23).

The agents decide the technical details, such as which engines back the connector core and whether DuckDB or MetricFlow adapters are part of it.
OPN-63.note: Dictated by Daniel in the review chat on 2026-10-26: "Daniel: 'if you send your own HTML rendered offline, then it should never support live data… unless you hooked it up to a URL, in which case… you should download it… you have to trust the person sending you the HTML anyhow, so that's fine… live connectors should be a standard for all the RichView servers… you need to build the connector core… CMS is not like a full CMS… both local and remote should offer a set of connectors you can set up. You can give specific people access to those connectors. Specific people manage those connectors, and then you can have a SQL code instead of… link to a specific CSV' (2026-10-26, live)".
